title: Without ends, bond distance is a ruler that reads the lattice's dimension
subject: Whether the smallest-knot distance of an infinite uniform law measures separation
conclusion: If a law's finitely supported moves are dense (no ends), every knot is chained at the moves' range, so bond distance grows linearly with separation and its balls recover the lattice's dimension from allowed states alone, with taxicab distance on the gauge plane and exactly t-s+1 along the atom thread. Per-variable nativity is not enough: Ledrappier's law plus a free field is native in every variable yet has knots joining points 2^k apart.
